text:
jess: Heads-up — seeing flaky okhttp cancellations on our Android SDK when devices enter battery-saver / doze mode. Retrofit calls just die with `IOException: canceled`. Happening on Android 12/13, especially when screen off and wifi/telephony toggles.

marco: ugh. which okhttp/retrofit versions? any repro app?

jess: okhttp 4.11 + retrofit 2.9 wrapper. native sample app repro is small — call to /v1/generate, token refresh occasionally races then request cancels. logs: 

```
2026-03-18 02:14:22.123 D/OkHttp: callStart: POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
2026-03-18 02:14:27.456 W/Network: Device entering DOZE; network callbacks delayed
2026-03-18 02:14:29.001 E/OkHttp: java.io.IOException: Canceled
    at okhttp3.internal.connection.ExchangeFinder.findConnection(ExchangeFinder.kt:...)
    at okhttp3.internal.connection.RealCall.execute(RealCall.kt:...)
Caused by: java.net.SocketException: Socket closed
```

jess: note: we had `retryOnConnectionFailure(true)` and `callTimeout(30s)` set. sometimes the cancellation happens before timeout and triggers our retry logic, which replays the request. if token refresh is racing, we get duplicate refreshes and 401 loop.

rachel: can you paste the OkHttp client config? are you using `ConnectionPool` tweaks or `pingInterval`? also does the sdk expose call cancellation to callers?

jess: current builder snippet: 

```
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .callTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build()
```

jess: we do expose `cancel()` via Call object but higher-level APIs hide the okhttp call. so app devs see generic failures.

akash: hypothesis: Doze causes network stack to drop sockets; Android signals app/process about network change which cancels the OkHttp call (SocketException), OkHttp surfaces as canceled vs timed out. Our retry logic treats cancellation like transient and retries immediately. when the device wakes, previous call completes/fails and the retried call duplicates work. If refresh token was in-flight, duplicates clash.

luis: makes sense. two mitigation ideas: 1) differentiate system-cancel vs user-cancel in SDK and do not auto-retry on system-induced cancellations; 2) add short jitter/backoff before retry when cancellation reason looks like Socket closed. also consider using `pingInterval` or HTTP/2 keepalives to avoid abrupt socket-close during short doze windows.

marco: agree. we should also surface a `FailureReason` enum to callers: TIMEOUT, IO_CANCELLED, USER_CANCELLED, NETWORK_LOST, etc. that lets app code do idempotency tokens.

rachel: i can reproduce on Pixel 5 in battery saver quickly. will attach logs to the issue. can someone make a minimal sample that toggles battery saver while a long poll runs?

jess: i'll drop a tiny sample app this afternoon. simple Activity: start request, toggle battery saver via adb, observe cancel.

akash: another quick fix: set `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for mobile clients and handle retries at a higher layer where we can detect idempotency. For now that might stop duplicate refresh races.

luis: also consider short-circuiting token refresh if another refresh is ongoing (singleflight pattern). that would prevent duplicate refresh regardless of retry behavior.

marco: good call. can we add a small test matrix: Android 11/12/13, battery-saver on/off, wifi->cell swap, okhttp 4.x? let's add results to the SDK parity tracker.

dev-bot: Issue created: DEX-4321 — "Android: OkHttp cancellations during Doze cause retry/refresh duplication" (<https://issues.redwood/DEX-4321>) :eyes:

jess: thanks — linking PRs when available. for the immediate SDK patch i'll try: disable retryOnConnectionFailure on mobile default + add singleflight for refresh + expose FailureReason.

rachel: :thumbsup: i'll validate on devices and paste logs in the issue.

marco: assign to eng-devx and mark as high for SDK stability in mobile onboarding docs.

jess: noted. will follow up with repro APK and minimal test steps.

luis: optional: document this in onboarding FAQ (battery-saver networking edgecases) so partners don't get surprised.

akash: also check whether WorkManager/foreground services change behavior — long-running background calls might need foreground service to avoid Doze cancellations.

jess: good idea. ok i'll update DEX-4321 with notes and ping infra if we need additional telemetry. thanks all.
